# Loading Packages 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1)
```

# Problem 1 

```{r}
#writing a function for a fixed group size
birthday_simulations = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE) 
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}

#setting up 10,000 simulations for each group size between 2 and 50

birthday_simulations_df = 
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared_birthday = map(group_size, birthday_simulations)
  ) |>
  unnest(shared_birthday)

birthday_probabilities_df =
  birthday_simulations_df |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(shared_birthday)
  )
```

```{r}
# creating plot
birthday_probabilities_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a Shared Birthday by Group Size",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of a Shared Birthday"
  )
```

The probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increased as group size increased. Approximately, when there were 23 people in a group, the probability was approximately 50%, even though there were 365 possible birthdays. When the group size was 50, the probability increased to around 97%. The curve is roughly S-shaped, which demonstrates that the probability increased for smaller groups, before increasing rapidly for larger groups, and beginning to level off as the curve approached 1.

# Problem 2

```{r}
#importing csv files
longitudinal_arms_df = 
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    data = map(path, read_csv)
  ) |>
  unnest(data)

#tidying data
longitudinal_tidy_df = 
  longitudinal_arms_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with ("week_"),
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |>
  separate(
    files, 
    into = c("arm", "subject_id"),
    sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    subject_id = str_replace(subject_id, ".csv", ""),
    week = as.numeric(str_replace(week, "week_", ""))
  )
```


```{r}
#Making the Spaghetti Plot
longitudinal_tidy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = observation,
             group = subject_id, color = arm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~arm, labeller = as_labeller(c(
    con = "Control",
    exp = "Experimental"
  ))) +
  scale_color_discrete(
    labels = c("Control", "Experimental")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Longitudinal Observations by Study Arm",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation",
    color = "Study Arm"
  )
```

The Spaghetti Plot shows the longitudinal observation of subjects in the control and experimental arms over an eight week period. Observations in the control arm fluctuate without a clear overall trend in direction. On the other hand, observations in the experimental arms generally increase over time. This suggests that the experimental arms shows an upward trend in observations compared to the relatively stable control arm.
